An approximation, not an animal\'s experience

AniVision shows an approximation of what a dog\'s or cat\'s cone cells might capture. It cannot show what a dog actually sees or experiences, and the same goes for a cat: that depends on the brain, not only on the eye.

People have three kinds of colour-sensitive cone cells. Dogs and cats have two, so they are generally thought to tell blues and yellows apart well but to confuse reds and greens, which look like muted yellows and browns. The Dog and Cat views apply that kind of colour mapping to the camera image.
Dogs and cats see less fine detail than people. The optional blur softens the image to hint at that. It is exaggerated on purpose so that the effect is visible on a phone screen.
Night boost brightens the shadows. It is an artistic effect to help show dim scenes, not a model of how dogs or cats see in the dark.

The cat\'s colour and blur are very similar to the dog\'s, so the two views look almost the same on their own. To hint at what is different about cats, the Cat view adds three artistic extras. They are not measurements. It brightens shadows a little, as an echo of cats\' better dim-light vision. When the blur is on, the blur grows towards the edges of the picture. And on phones with an ultra-wide lens it zooms out to the widest view, as a hint of a cat\'s wide field of view.
AniVision uses the camera only to show the live view and take photos. Photos are saved to Pictures/AniVision on your device. Nothing is collected or sent anywhere.
